sources.title: Fogg, B.J. — Tiny Habits / the Fogg Behavior Model (B=MAP)
sources.used_for: Behaviour = Motivation x Ability x Prompt, multiplicative not additive; ability sub-factors include 'brain cycles' and 'non-routine'
sources.note: Verified by web search 2026-10-06; multiple independent summaries agree on the multiplicative model and the three prompt types (spark/facilitator/signal).

sources.title: Ostrom, Elinor — Governing the Commons (1990), eight design principles
sources.used_for: Boundaries, proportionality, collective choice, monitoring, graduated sanctions, cheap conflict resolution, nested enterprise, recognised self-determination

sources.title: Elster, Jon — Ulysses Unbound (2000)
sources.used_for: Constitutions as precommitment devices; Elster's own later partial repudiation of the clean individual/collective self-binding analogy
sources.note: Verified by web search 2026-10-06 — multiple summaries confirm Elster revisits and partially retracts the precommitment framing in the book's second part.

sources.title: Majors, Charity — observability-driven development, 'production is the only truth'
sources.used_for: If you didn't instrument it, you don't know it broke; deploying to production is the beginning of understanding, not the end
sources.note: Verified by web search 2026-10-06. Exact phrase not found verbatim; underlying claim confirmed across multiple independent summaries of her talks and writing.

sources.title: Scott, James C. — Seeing Like a State (1998); Weapons of the Weak (1985)
sources.used_for: Legibility, metis vs. techne, high modernism
sources.note: Not independently re-verified by web search this session; relying on established, widely-taught content of these two books.

sources.title: Norman, Don — The Design of Everyday Things
sources.used_for: Slips vs. mistakes, affordances/signifiers, 'human error is usually a design error'
sources.note: Not independently re-verified by web search this session; relying on established, widely-taught content of this book.

sources.title: Schneier, Bruce — security economics, attack trees, 'security theater'
sources.used_for: Who benefits from ambiguity; a control that cannot in principle be audited is worse than a known vulnerability
sources.note: Not independently re-verified by web search this session; relying on established, widely-published content across Schneier's books and essays.
